trust_boundaries.name: Untrusted content into the model context

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT treat content retrieved from external sources ... as trusted instructions
MUST NOT accept or act on instructions from anyone other than its single owner-operator
Any third party who reaches the agent through a connected channel but is not the owner.

threats.summary: Fetched web pages, MCP server output and arbitrary file contents enter the prompt with no provenance label or trust tier, and the repository's only injection filter is never called and would pass a match through unchanged.

The third-party notification embeds 500 characters of a stranger's raw message and appends it to the conversation history, so attacker-authored prose is in the model's context on the owner's next turn.
A stranger messaging a connected platform account gets a session opened and their text treated as owner direction.

remit_rules.excerpt: sandboxed code and shell execution; web search and fetch; ... Any tool or capability ... outside this baseline is a trust-expansion finding.
Any action that modifies persistent state ... requires owner approval before execution.
Any irreversible or externally-visible action ... requires explicit owner approval before execution.
Host command and code execution MUST be gated by owner approval and MUST NOT inherit the parent process environment
MUST NOT auto-approve, self-grant, or downgrade the approval requirement for any action above its declared permission tier.
Any outbound destination, service, or account the owner has not explicitly connected or authorized.
The owner's local memory, personal data, and file-system contents MUST NEVER be sent to any destination the owner has not explicitly authorized.

threats.summary: The model's next action after ingesting external content can be run_shell, which passes the string to the host shell with shell=True and a copy of the parent environment carrying the provider API keys — no approval gate, denylist or per-command policy exists on that path.

The four documented permission tiers are written, range-checked and displayed but never read at execution time, and add_action_sets sits in the always-available core set, so scheduled and proactive work runs unsupervised and the model can widen its own action inventory mid-task.
74 irreversible integration actions with arbitrary recipients and an HTTP client that will POST a body to any public host are reachable with no destination allowlist and no approval step.
An irreversible send is re-executed after a crash or a redelivery, repeating the side effect.
threats.remainder: the ledger only dedups a repeat — it never gates a first execution, and a reworded call hashes differently and slips the guard

remit_rules.excerpt: The LLM provider the owner configured (one of the supported providers, local or remote).

threats.summary: Whatever the loop has gathered — credential-file contents pulled by the unconfined reader, memory chunks, third-party message text — leaves the host inside the prompt, and the same prompt and response are written verbatim to a local SQLite store; a sweep of the LLM interface, the context engine and the logging stack found no redaction or field-allowlist layer anywhere.
An action or retry loop burns the owner's provider spend without bound.

trust_boundaries.name: Credentials at rest and injected at deploy

remit_rules.excerpt: No user-data token, bot token, or server-side API key may be embedded or shipped in the distributed code.
Credentials and tokens at rest MUST be stored with owner-only access and MUST NOT be world-readable.

threats.summary: Live OAuth client secrets for five providers plus a Telegram api_id/api_hash ship in the source tree as base64 fragments joined at runtime, with build helpers to mint more and a docstring naming evasion of GitHub scanning as the purpose.

Provider API keys delivered to the agent container through env_file are copied wholesale into the environment of every model-authored shell command, so the credential boundary the remit requires around host execution does not exist.
Stored OAuth and bot tokens are readable by other local accounts on the owner's machine.

trust_boundaries.name: Local stores readable into the agent's context

remit_rules.excerpt: credential and configuration stores MUST be excluded from indexing, retrieval, and summarization by default

threats.summary: read_file takes any absolute host path behind an isfile() check alone, so .credentials/<platform>.json and app/config/settings.json — the stores the agent's own documentation names as holding OAuth tokens, bot tokens and API keys — read straight into model context alongside grep_files and find_files.

The ChromaDB collection re-indexes the agent file system whenever a file changes with no authenticated write path, no validation and no hidden-content detection, and memory_search returns the chunks with nothing distinguishing owner-authored notes from ingested external text.

remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT directly edit harness-managed state files — distilled memory, the append-only event log, conversation history, task history, and the memory index
A complex/multi-step task MUST obtain explicit owner approval before it is finalized or ended.

threats.summary: write_file and stream_edit accept any absolute path with no protected-path list, so SOUL.md, AGENT.md and MEMORY.md — the files loaded into context at the start of every session — can be rewritten from inside a task, turning one injected instruction into a standing one for every future session.

trust_boundaries.name: Network-reachable surfaces the agent stands up

remit_rules.excerpt: Any server or listener the agent starts ... MUST bind to loopback/localhost and MUST NOT be exposed to the public network without explicit owner approval.

threats.summary: The Living UI sidecar proxy and every scaffolded app backend bind 0.0.0.0 with wildcard CORS and no authentication dependency, so on a café or office network anyone on the LAN reaches applications built on the owner's data.

The desktop container publishes its remote-desktop port on every host interface with a literal default password and seccomp disabled, handing anyone who reaches it a graphical session on the machine the agent drives.
A Living UI backend calls the agent's own bridge routes (integration proxy, LLM and VLM passthrough) to act with the owner's connected credentials.
threats.remainder: a Bearer bridge token is the only check, and the sidecar sitting in front of those apps still accepts any origin on any interface

remit_rules.excerpt: a server whose launch resolves an unpinned upstream package on each start is outside this closure regardless of who enabled it

threats.summary: Both default-enabled MCP servers launch through npx with no version pin — the filesystem server scoped to "." and Playwright pinned to the mutable @latest tag — so each start fetches and executes whatever the registry currently serves, and their tools feed straight into the agent's context.

All 55 Python dependencies are unpinned with no lockfile and no SBOM, so two installs can resolve different LLM SDK, vector-store and browser-automation code and no deployment can answer which versions it runs.

The cloudflared binary is downloaded from a mutable "latest" release URL and executed with no checksum, signature or version pin, in the component whose whole job is publishing a local service to the internet.

remit_rules.excerpt: Stored credentials, OAuth/bot tokens, and LLM API keys MUST NEVER be printed to chat, written to logs, or transmitted to any destination.
Routine actions and decisions MUST be recorded to the durable event/action log for audit, without interrupting the owner.

threats.summary: Every loguru sink is added with backtrace and diagnose enabled, so a propagating exception in an integration or LLM call path renders local variables — where provider keys, OAuth tokens and bot tokens live — into the log file, and no sink installs a redaction filter.

Nothing alerts when a high-impact action runs: the ledger and logs stay on local disk with no exporter and no alert hook, so detection depends on the owner opening a file that anything with host shell access can also edit.

notes.lane_fit: Two strains. Living UI is one remit capability whose parts land in different lanes — the scaffolding/sharing tool is agent-invoked (tools_mcp) while the app and sidecar listeners it starts are owner-facing web surfaces (client_adapters); modelled as one tools_mcp node named for the manager that creates them, with the listener evidence attached. And the log sinks and the irreversible-action ledger are placed in external_deploy per the lane table's telemetry-sink line even though nothing ever leaves the host — that locality is itself finding PRAX-2026-08-12-016.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergences from the stored tags, KB taking precedence. Substantive: (1) PRAX-2026-08-12-008 stored ASI07 — the Agentic KB scopes ASI07 to inter-agent communication and no agent-to-agent channel is involved in a uvicorn 0.0.0.0 bind, so the threat is tagged null rather than forced into a code; (2) PRAX-2026-08-12-007 stored ASI02 — the KB reserves ASI02 for misuse in action of a non-exec tool, and this finding's evidence is a gate/grant gap (no destination allowlist, no approval), so LLM03 is primary under the 'ungated consequential capability' row, with the exfiltration consequence unchanged. Primary-selection only, not retags: PRAX-2026-08-12-003 stores ASI10 and LLM03 — the compound table makes LLM03 primary with ASI10 riding as the standing-autonomy co-tag; PRAX-2026-08-12-009 stores ASI04 and LLM04 — the unverified-MCP-install row makes LLM04 primary with ASI04 co-tag. Components cited but folded rather than given their own node, to hold the size target: the CLI adapter, the sub-agent runner and registry, the scheduler and proactive managers, the skill loader and the 195-skill corpus (folded into the orchestrator), the OmniParser Gradio service and the GUI computer-use handler (folded into the Docker deployment node), the llm_calls prompt-capture store (folded into the LLM call layer), and the session router. Edgeless nodes, one clause each: prompt-sanitizer-py-control is dead code with no call site; agent-md-control is prose governance no code path reads; requirements-txt-deploy-surface is repo posture. Both posture boundaries (supply-chain, control-plane-exposure) carry no crossing edges by the same logic.
